newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CEPA in talks to fund Indonesia project.
newsitem.headline: CEPA in talks to fund Indonesia project.

text.p: Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) said on Thursday it was in discussion with banks for a project financing package funding its Tanjung Jati B Plant in Indonesia.

"CEPA has been in discussion with seven international banks, which are involved in the financing of the Tanjung Jati B Plant, for a project financing package to fund the cost of the Tanjung Jati B Plant which will satisfy the payment condition for the Contingent Entitlement," CEPA said in a joint statement.
Last month, Hopewell Holdings Ltd agreed to the sale of a major portion of its 60.4 percent interest in CEPA to Southern Co in a move which could lead to the privatisation and delisting of CEPA.
Southern proposed two options to CEPA shareholders. The first is a straightforward offer of HK$18.5 per CEPA share.
The second option offers shareholders one new CEPA share, plus cash of HK$69.50, plus a "contingency entitlement" of an additional HK$8.00 for every five CEPA shares held.
The contingency payment depends on the achievement of limited recourse debt for a power plant in Indonesia and a final dividend of HK$0.15 per share.

CEPA said in the statement published on Thursday that "the discussions with such lenders include certain conditions which, until they are met, will not satisfy the payment condition for the Contingent Entitlement."
"CEPA will continue its discussion with lenders regarding the financing arrangements of the Tanjung Jati B Plant," the statement said.
